title: Eneo Flows runs reliably and remains easy to change
description:
TL;DR: Make Eneo Flow proper safe to operate in production and straightforward to change without creating parallel ownership with Flow AI Builder. This epic owns Flow runtime, persistence, API/client, UI, administrator-controlled retention, health, recovery, release evidence, and maintainability work; AI Builder internals remain out of scope.

## Product decision

Flow history, runs, evidence, files, and related records are preserved by default. Existing duration values never imply deletion. Organization administrators may configure one complete mode-plus-days policy at Organization, Space, or Flow scope; the most-specific complete policy wins. `preserve` requires an explicit on-demand purge, `review_required` requires approval of a bounded preview, and `automatic` is available only after a separate explicit activation and safety implementation. Every deletion path reuses the same bounded, retry-safe, audited purge owner.

## Success Criteria

- Authored secrets never persist plaintext, and existing exposure has a verified recovery path.
- Scheduled maintenance never purges Flow-owned history or content unless an Organization administrator explicitly activates an effective `automatic` policy after the required preview, grace, audit, and recovery gates; `preserve` and `review_required` never auto-delete.
- Manual, review-approved, and explicitly automatic purges share one preview, authorization, execution, protected-reference, recovery, and immutable-receipt contract.
- Run recovery, external delivery, publication concurrency, worker health, and dead-letter recovery have explicit tested outcomes.
- Canonical owners replace duplicate validation, status, evidence, and frontend state paths without generic new layers.
- The exact release candidate passes code, migration, failure, security, image, staging, and rollback gates.
- Flow AI Builder consumes stabilized Flow contracts through a coordinated baseline rather than conflicting edits.
- Each implementation slice has behavior/contract tests, rollback or recovery notes, and a reviewable deletion/consolidation boundary.

title: Rehearse Flow database upgrades and recovery boundaries
description:
TL;DR: Prove the exact Flow migration graph against a production-like snapshot from the oldest supported revision, including lock budgets, parity, interruption, and fix-forward recovery.

## Problem

Passing an empty-database migration test does not establish safe upgrade behavior for large existing Flow tables. Applied versus unreleased revisions also determine whether cleanup is legal.

## Canonical owner and approach

Alembic remains the migration owner. Classify each Flow revision by deployment state. Correct unreleased history before release; fix forward if applied anywhere meaningful. Do not rewrite migration files based only on style.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Oldest supported deployed revision is named and restored with representative row counts/payload sizes.
- Upgrade to the exact candidate head succeeds and schema parity matches a clean database.
- Lock duration, statement duration, disk growth, and critical query plans are recorded and accepted.
- Orphan preflights precede new constraints; large-table validation/index choices fit the lock budget.
- Interrupted migration/restart behavior is tested where applicable.
- Downgrade is either rehearsed or explicitly refused with a documented fix-forward/restore boundary.
- Backup restore and application/image compatibility boundaries are recorded.
- No applied revision is rewritten.

## Tests and validation

- cd backend && uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_alembic_migration_graph.py
- Run alembic upgrade from the restored oldest-supported snapshot to candidate head.
- Compare schema catalogs with a clean candidate database.
- Capture EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) for run history, stale recovery, outbox claims, evidence export, and explicit purge selection.

## Risk and recovery

Migration rehearsal uses disposable restored data with no production credentials. Recovery is restore or fix-forward according to the recorded boundary; never attempt an unproven downgrade in production.

## Out of scope

No speculative indexes, ORM replacement, or aesthetic migration squashing.

## Evidence

Supplied review lines 247-259 and 865-872 define the migration safety boundary.
Confidence: high.

title: Prove Flow runtime recovery at durable failure points
Measure Flow workloads against declared release budgets
description:
TL;DR: Measure only the three changed or launch-critical Flow hot paths before release; defer a broad performance program until production evidence exists.

## Problem

The original draft profiles nearly every Flow workload before launch. That dilutes the gate and turns speculation into P0 work. The release needs bounded proof for changed/high-risk paths, not a universal benchmark campaign.

## Canonical owner and approach

Measure:
1. run-history list at 50/200 rows with typical and maximum payloads;
2. explicit administrator purge at representative batch scale, including shared files and blockers;
3. queue/outbox lag and claim throughput under the release topology.

Record exact SHA, images, config, dataset, hardware, response bytes, DB time/plan, lock wait, browser heap where relevant, worker CPU/RSS, and p95/p99. This narrow receipt is intentionally a P0 release gate because final candidate certification depends on it; broader performance work remains post-launch. Create optimization work only for failed budgets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Owners predeclare acceptable release ceilings for the three named paths.
- Results are reproducible and machine-readable.
- Run-history evidence separates batched enrichment from full-row payload weight and offset pagination.
- Purge evidence proves bounded transactions, lock deferral, progress, and manual resume.
- Queue/outbox evidence proves lag/throughput under expected and burst load.
- Any index/refactor cites a failed ceiling and before/after correctness evidence.
- The broader workload list is explicitly post-launch, not silently required by certification.

## Tests and validation

Run the three workloads against exact candidate images and production-like PostgreSQL/storage/broker topology with enough samples for stable percentiles. Retain raw data plus gate verdict.

## Risk and recovery

Use isolated staging and bounded data; stop before threatening shared capacity.

## Out of scope

No speculative indexes, ORM replacement, shared-session provider parallelism, Python micro-optimization, or universal performance project.

## Evidence

Reviewed tree:
- backend/src/eneo/flows/infrastructure/flow_run_repo.py:513-545 selects full rows.
- backend/src/eneo/flows/application/flow_run_service.py:716-776 performs batched enrichment.
- frontend/apps/web/src/lib/features/flows/components/flowRunHistoryState.ts:85-96 documents the 200 MiB theoretical exposure.
Confidence: high.

title: Certify the exact Eneo Flows release candidate
description:
TL;DR: Freeze one candidate and authorize production only when all dependency receipts refer to that exact identity. Certification references evidence; it does not rerun or own implementation/failure work.

## Problem

Earlier passing suites are not receipts for the final candidate, and duplicated staging campaigns create conflicting evidence owners.

## Canonical owner and approach

The release lead owns one immutable identity ledger: parent/candidate SHA, migration head, generated-client hash, backend/frontend image digests, SBOM/attestations, config version, topology, and rollback pair. Consume dependency receipts without repeating their campaigns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Worktree is clean and parent/candidate relationship and exact diff are reviewed.
- Full backend/frontend/generated-client/type/import/build/image/security gates pass at the exact SHA.
- Credential/encryption closure is signed off.
- Migration, runtime-failure, health/runbook, browser-authoring, explicit-purge, dead-letter-redrive, and narrowed hot-path receipts all name the same candidate/images/config or are rerun only when invalidated.
- One staging smoke proves composition of authoring, publish, run, review, result/evidence, purge preview/start/status, redrive command availability, and restart recovery without duplicating the failure matrix.
- Rollback images, database compatibility, restore procedure, owners, and stop conditions are recorded.
- No waiver can bypass webhook atomicity, automatic-purge prohibition, credential revocation, tenant isolation, or data-loss safeguards.
- Verdict is explicit go/no-go.

## Tests and validation

Run full CI/release commands from the frozen candidate and attach immutable dependency receipts. Any SHA/image/config/migration change invalidates affected evidence.

## Risk and recovery

Never deploy a different identity pair. Failed gate means no-go; recovery uses the recorded rollback/restore boundary.

## Out of scope

No implementation, architecture cleanup, repeated failure campaign, or broad benchmark work.

## Evidence

Supplied review lines 351-371, 850-897, and 1003-1059 defines exact-candidate certification.
Confidence: high.
notes: Release certification must record security acceptance of the administrator-controlled retention trade-off: Flow debug and provider evidence can persist indefinitely until manual purge. title: Prove active Flow state survives reload and reconnect
description:
TL;DR: Extend the stable browser baseline after launch so reload or reconnect during an active/review-paused run recovers canonical server state without duplicate action or stale UI.

## Problem

The P0 authoring journey proves the primary path, but not interruption recovery. Polling generations and persisted runtime state should make reload safe; one focused journey must prove it.

## Canonical owner and approach

Deepen the existing Flow Playwright spec and current run-history/detail state owners. Test observable recovery; do not add a second state store or offline framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reload during running resumes polling without duplicate run creation.
- Reload during review restores the same checkpoint and permitted actions.
- Reconnect after a transient backend failure discards stale responses and converges on current server state.
- Terminal state stops polling and survives a second reload.
- Cancel/review/resume actions are not replayed.
- The test uses deterministic network/state barriers, not sleeps.

## Tests and validation

- cd frontend && bun run --filter '@eneo/web' test
- cd frontend && bun run check

## Out of scope

No offline mode, generic sync engine, or AI Builder state.

## Evidence

Confidence: high.

title: Serve sparse Flow run summaries with stable cursor pagination
description:
TL;DR: Replace full-row run-history pages with a dedicated summary projection and stable cursor contract while preserving detail/evidence endpoints.

## Problem

The list query selects full FlowRuns rows and the frontend retains up to 200 full payloads. Batched enrichment avoids N+1, but full JSON payload weight and offset pagination remain the largest confirmed scalability opportunity.

## Canonical owner and approach

FlowRunRepository owns a concrete summary projection; FlowRunService exposes a typed FlowRunSummary page. Detail, evidence, files, and provider usage remain their existing owners. Add keyset pagination on (created_at, id); keep the old offset contract only until a versioned generated-client migration completes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Summary selects no full input/output/error JSON, evidence, provider calls, or file descriptors.
- It includes only identity/version, status capabilities, compact principal/timestamps/revision, bounded error/output summary, and review-required indicator.
- No N+1 queries.
- Detail loads on selection.
- Max-payload list response bytes fall at least 90% from the measured baseline.
- Cursor pagination is stable under concurrent inserts and deterministic ties.
- API p95/DB/serialization/browser heap at 50 and 200 rows meet the budget from flows-1z1.12.
- Generated types drive frontend migration.
- Old offset clients retain behavior until explicit deprecation/removal.

## Tests and validation

PostgreSQL projection/cursor concurrency tests, API/OpenAPI/client compatibility tests, frontend state/component tests, and before/after measurement.

- cd backend && uv run pytest -q tests/integration/flows/test_flow_run_listing_and_evidence_measurement.py tests/unit/test_flow_openapi_contract.py

## Risk and recovery

Add the summary contract before migrating consumers. Roll back frontend to old list while retaining the additive endpoint; delete compatibility only in a later versioned migration.

## Out of scope

title: Make Flow control-envelope corruption explicit
description:
TL;DR: Add typed, versioned parsers and explicit corrupt/unsupported behavior only for persisted JSON envelopes that control review, rerun, dispatch, or resume decisions.

## Problem

Arbitrary user/provider JSON is correctly flexible, but some internally owned control envelopes can make malformed state look absent or alter runtime decisions.

## Canonical owner and approach

Each lifecycle owner defines its own typed parser and versions; no generic JSON utility. Roll out review checkpoint first, then rerun and remaining dispatch/error metadata only where current parsers are insufficient.

## Acceptance Criteria

For each selected envelope:
- inventory stored shapes and supported versions;
- add one typed parser with explicit absent/corrupt/unsupported outcomes;
- preserve read compatibility before strict writes;
- emit sanitized corruption diagnostics and operator behavior;
- add fixtures for every supported historical version;
- backfill/migrate only after read compatibility and corruption inventory;
- malformed state never silently means “not configured.”

## Tests and validation

Parser fixtures, database reads of supported/corrupt/unsupported rows, runtime review/resume/rerun behavior, strict typing, and migration preflight if required.

- cd backend && uv run pytest -q tests/integration/flows
- cd backend && uv run ruff check src/eneo && uv run pyright

## Risk and recovery

Strict writes can strand old data if reads are not compatible first. Roll back enforcement while retaining tolerant typed reads and diagnostics.

## Out of scope

No relationalization of arbitrary user/provider JSON and no generic envelope framework.

## Evidence

Supplied review lines 209-234 and 531-549 identifies internally owned control envelopes as the bounded gap.
Confidence: medium-high pending stored-shape inventory.

title: Deepen Flow transactions at named runtime checkpoints
description:
TL;DR: After release behavior is proven, move one durable executor transition at a time behind a behavior-named persistence operation with crash-state tests.

## Problem

The executor is inherently orchestration-heavy and contains many explicit commit/rollback checkpoints. The risk is reviewability and accidental partial state, not its line count alone.

## Canonical owner and approach

Extract only a transition whose atomic outcome can be stated independently, such as start_step_attempt or complete_step_result_and_enqueue_webhook. The concrete repository/service operation owns one transaction outcome; migrate callers and delete the old inline path in the same slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Select one checkpoint based on flows-1z1.11 failure evidence.
- State preconditions, persisted postcondition, idempotency, conflict, crash, retry, and audit/outbox behavior.
- One concrete operation owns the transaction; executor calls it without duplicate writes.
- Injected crash tests assert persisted state, not private calls.
- Commit/rollback count and branching decrease for the selected lifecycle.
- No facade preserves the old path.

## Tests and validation

Run targeted executor/runtime/PostgreSQL contracts and the matching failure case from flows-1z1.11, plus Ruff/Pyright.

## Risk and recovery

Keep each PR to one checkpoint. Revert the moved operation and caller together if behavior differs.

## Out of scope

No generic unit of work, repository base, handler-owned transactions, state-machine framework, or event sourcing.

## Evidence

Reviewed tree backend/src/eneo/flows/runtime/executor.py is 2,476 lines and contains explicit commit/rollback checkpoints at multiple lifecycle phases; supplied review lines 491-512 recommends named transitions, not a rewrite.
Confidence: high for hotspot, medium for first checkpoint until failure evidence.

title: Give selected-run state one frontend controller
description:
TL;DR: Consolidate selected-run identity, detail refresh, stale-response control, actions, and reconciliation into one concrete controller while keeping route and views narrow.

## Problem

Run-history state is already robust, but FlowRunsTable still owns selection, refresh integration, redispatch, cancellation, and rendering across a large component. This increases change cost for interruption and action behavior.

## Canonical owner and approach

Add one concrete selected-run controller in the Flow feature. It consumes the existing history state and generated client. FlowRunsTable/detail components emit intents and render; the route remains composition/permission/tab owner. Delete moved state/action paths in the same slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

The controller owns:
- selected run identity;
- detail refresh timer and stale-response generation/cancellation;
- cancel/redispatch/review actions;
- optimistic reconciliation into history;
- terminal stop conditions.

Views contain no duplicate timers/API orchestration. Route owns no selected-run domain state. Component behavior and reload/reconnect tests remain green.

## Tests and validation

- cd frontend && bun run --filter '@eneo/web' test
- cd frontend && bun run check
- Run Flow Playwright lifecycle/reload specs.

## Risk and recovery

Avoid a large route rewrite. Move one ownership cluster with characterization tests and revert controller plus callers together.

## Out of scope

No generic global store, Flow manager, or AI Builder state consolidation.

## Evidence

Reviewed tree frontend/apps/web/src/lib/features/flows/components/FlowRunsTable.svelte is 932 lines and owns selectedRunId plus redispatch/cancel actions around lines 93 and 191-361; flowRunHistoryState.ts should remain the history owner.
Confidence: high.

title: Make every significant Flow action durably auditable
description:
TL;DR: Every security-, lifecycle-, and data-significant Eneo Flow action must leave a trustworthy, redacted audit record with the initiating principal, outcome, and relevant Flow/run context. Reuse the existing AuditService and transactional Flow audit outbox; fill concrete coverage and failure-semantics gaps without creating a second audit framework. Preserve only the minimum current tenant attribution/isolation needed for correctness because multi-tenancy is a retiring direction.

## Parent epic

`flows-1z1` — Eneo Flows runs reliably and remains easy to change.

## Problem

Flow audit logging already has strong pieces, but coverage and durability are inconsistent. Authoring actions, terminal/review transitions, evidence access, runtime file operations, outbound calls, and transcription do not all share an explicit coverage contract or failure policy. That makes it difficult for an administrator to reconstruct who changed, accessed, executed, or deleted Flow data, and lets important new endpoints ship without an audit decision.

Concrete gaps include a runtime-file upload path with no corresponding audit event, a template signed-URL path with no access event, and best-effort outbound/transcription logging that silently continues when audit delivery is absent or fails. The issue is not a missing generic abstraction; it is incomplete use of existing owners and unspecified failure modes.

## Canonical owners and proposed approach

Create one reviewable audit-coverage matrix for public Flow mutations, sensitive reads, runtime lifecycle transitions, and destructive operator actions. For each action, name its existing canonical owner, event, actor, outcome, required metadata, durability, idempotency behavior, and audit-failure behavior.

Reuse and deepen existing owners:

- `AuditService` and `AuditMetadata.standard` for authoring/admin actions and sensitive reads where synchronous audit semantics are appropriate;
- `FlowRunAuditOutboxRepository` in the same database transaction for run terminalization, review checkpoints, retries/redispatch, and future destructive purge transitions;
- `flow_trace_audit` for fail-closed evidence and artifact access;
- existing `ActionType`, `ActorType`, `Outcome`, principal attribution, and redaction conventions.

Fill the matrix's direct gaps at those owners. At minimum, cover runtime input upload, template signed-URL minting, and any other public Flow mutation or sensitive download that currently lacks an event. Decide whether outbound HTTP and transcription events are compliance-required: if required, make their persistence durable without blocking external execution on the audit sink; if not, document and test their explicitly lower assurance level. Do not leave silent `None` or broad-catch behavior as an undocumented accident.

Keep metadata bounded and redacted: tenant id while the current model requires it, actor type/id/API-key id, Flow/run/step/file ids, action, outcome, reason or error classification, operation/correlation/idempotency key where applicable, and no prompt, document content, credentials, signed URLs, raw provider payloads, or secrets.

Multi-tenancy is deliberately minimal: preserve current tenant attribution, tenant-scoped lookup, and a focused cross-tenant isolation regression. Do not add tenant policy layers, tenant-specific abstractions, generalized tenancy middleware, or a broad tenant test matrix.

## Acceptance criteria

- One maintained coverage contract inventories all public Flow mutations and security-sensitive reads, including authoring, publish/unpublish, template/runtime files, run creation/lifecycle, review/edit/resume/cancel, retries/redispatch, evidence/artifact/package access, outbound delivery, and explicit purge.
- Every matrix row names the canonical code owner, action type, actor/principal, outcome, bounded metadata, durability level, idempotency behavior, and failure behavior.
- Missing significant actions emit an existing or narrowly added `ActionType`; no generic event-name bag or parallel audit service is introduced.
- Runtime and destructive state transitions enqueue their audit record in the same transaction through the existing Flow audit outbox. A failed outbox insert prevents the protected transition from committing.
- Evidence and other designated sensitive reads remain fail-closed when their required audit record cannot be persisted.
- Lower-risk authoring/read actions have an explicit, tested audit-failure policy rather than silently inheriting whichever logging call a router happens to use.
- Runtime input upload and template signed-URL minting record the actual authenticated principal, Flow/file context, and outcome without storing file contents or signed URLs.
- HTTP outbound and transcription audit semantics are explicitly decided and tested; missing audit infrastructure and sink failure cannot silently erase compliance-required events.
- Retries and duplicate delivery do not create misleading duplicate business events; audit delivery remains idempotent and observable.
- Current tenant id and tenant-scoped lookup remain correct, with one focused cross-tenant attribution/isolation regression; no new multi-tenancy architecture is added.
- The future explicit purge workflow from `flows-1z1.3` records requester, reason, eligibility snapshot, counts/bytes, outcome, and receipt identity through these existing owners.
- Dead-letter recovery remains owned by `flows-1z1.6`; this task does not implement another redrive path.
- Audit metadata and operator/API responses contain no secret, credential, signed URL, document content, prompt content, or raw provider payload.

## Tests and validation

- Add a table-driven contract test that maps each significant public Flow operation to its required audit action and failure semantics without mocking internal helper wiring.
- Add integration tests for runtime upload and template signed-URL audit attribution, bounded metadata, success outcome, and audit-unavailable behavior.
- Add transactional failure-injection tests proving terminal/review/destructive state cannot commit without its required outbox row.
- Keep evidence-access audit-unavailable tests fail-closed.
- Add retry/idempotency coverage for outbox delivery and one focused cross-tenant attribution/isolation case.
- Run: `cd backend && uv run pytest -q tests/integration/flows tests/unit tests/unittests`
- Run: `cd backend && uv run ruff check src/eneo tests && uv run pyright`
- Run: `python3 scripts/check_route_metadata.py --repo-root . --all`

## Risk and recovery

Making too many low-value events synchronous can reduce availability; leaving compliance-required events best-effort creates an incomplete record. The coverage matrix must classify the boundary before code changes. Roll back individual event additions at their canonical owner, but do not weaken transactional audit for lifecycle/destructive changes or fail-closed audit for sensitive evidence access.

## Out of scope

- No generic audit framework, event bus, plugin system, pass-through audit service, or second outbox.
- No audit dashboard redesign, analytics pipeline, SIEM integration, or bulk export project.
- No new multi-tenancy architecture or investment in tenant-specific product features.
- No dead-letter operator command; `flows-1z1.6` owns it.
- No explicit purge transport; `flows-1z1.3` owns it and consumes this audit contract.
- No Flow AI Builder audit expansion unless a shared Flow-proper operation directly crosses this contract.

## Evidence

- `backend/src/eneo/audit/domain/action_types.py:108-137` already owns a substantial Flow action vocabulary.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/application/flow_run_terminalization.py:230-261` inserts terminal audit outbox state with the lifecycle transition.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/infrastructure/flow_run_review_checkpoint_repo.py:409-439` transitions review state and inserts its outbox row in one session transaction.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/api/flow_trace_audit.py:24-94` correctly denies sensitive evidence access when required audit logging is unavailable.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/api/flow_upload_router.py:256-292` stores a runtime input file without an audit call, while deletion is audited at lines 343-393.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/api/flow_template_router.py:329-354` mints a template signed URL without an access event, while upload/delete are audited at lines 181-221 and 259-298.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/runtime/http_audit.py:55-96` and `backend/src/eneo/flows/runtime/transcription_runtime.py:118-168` treat missing/failing audit services as best-effort without a documented assurance classification.

Confidence: high.

title: Preserve Flow data until an administrator requests purging
description:
TL;DR: Remove every scheduled destructive Flow retention action. Flow history and content remain intact by default; policy values describe eligibility but never trigger deletion on a timer.

## Problem

The reviewed tree runs a daily retention job and automatically purges Flow run history, abandoned runtime uploads, soft-deleted template assets, debug evidence, and delivered audit-outbox rows. This conflicts with the approved product rule that administrators decide when Flow data is purged.

## Canonical owner and approach

Keep the platform retention worker for unrelated platform data, but delete its Flow-destructive calls. Keep Flow eligibility resolution for explicit preview. Do not add a replacement scheduler or compatibility fallback.

Reuse:
- FlowRunHistoryPurgeRepository for later explicit, reference-safe deletion;
- existing tenant/Space/Flow policy values as eligibility inputs;
- existing read-only health/count queries.

Delete:
- scheduled calls that purge or redact Flow-owned data;
- generated-client, API, docs, UI, and test promises that a policy change causes deletion on the next pass;
- the automatic-deletion control model in the stale retention-governance E2E and component tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No cron, worker startup, health task, or policy update invokes Flow run-history purge, debug-evidence redaction, abandoned-upload purge, soft-deleted template-asset purge, delivered Flow audit-outbox deletion, or Flow finalization.
- Flow history, evidence, files, uploads, and related records survive indefinitely until an authorized explicit purge request.
- Non-null retention settings only affect preview eligibility; null remains “not eligible.”
- Read-only counts, storage growth warnings, and capacity alerts may run automatically but cannot mutate Flow data.
- Non-Flow platform retention behavior is unchanged.
- frontend/apps/web/tests/flow-retention-governance.spec.ts and frontend/apps/web/src/routes/(app)/admin/flow-settings/flow-settings-page.svelte.test.ts are deleted/replaced where they encode automatic deletion; no parallel stale suite remains.
- English/Swedish copy, OpenAPI, generated client, docs, and tests consistently describe administrator-controlled purging.
- The product/security owner explicitly signs the storage-limitation trade-off: debug/provider evidence configured for time-based redaction will now persist until manual purge.
- No hidden scheduled fallback remains.

## Tests and validation

- cd backend && uv run pytest -q tests/unittests/data_retention/test_data_retention_worker.py tests/integration/test_flow_runtime_retention_cleanup.py
- cd backend && uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_flow_openapi_contract.py
- cd frontend && bun run --filter '@eneo/web' test
- cd frontend && bun run check

Add a unit contract that fails if the scheduled worker calls any Flow-destructive method, plus an integration contract proving an eligible terminal run, debug envelope, abandoned upload, template asset, and delivered outbox row survive a scheduled pass.

## Risk and recovery

Accepted risk is storage growth until an administrator purges. Monitor eligible counts/bytes and capacity without deletion. Rollback may restore a scheduler only after a new explicit product decision; it is never an operational fallback.

## Out of scope

Do not disable unrelated conversation, app-run, session, or Builder retention. Do not build administrator purge transport in this slice.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a non-null Flow retention policy and create eligible terminal run history, debug evidence, an abandoned runtime upload, a soft-deleted template asset, and a delivered audit-outbox row.
2. Run the scheduled `cleanup_old_data` pass.
3. Observe Flow-owned records or content being deleted or redacted without an administrator requesting a purge.

title: Make Flow retention a complete administrator-owned policy
description:
TL;DR: Replace days-only Flow retention with one complete Organization → Space → Flow policy so administrators can choose preservation or review without coupling operational governance to Flow authoring. Existing values remain non-destructive.

## Problem and operator impact

Flow retention currently stores only days, borrows generic Space conversation retention, and lets ordinary Flow editors change the Flow override through the draft definition interface. Published Flows cannot be updated there. The system cannot express whether eligible history is preserved or requires human review, and partial inheritance would make future automatic deletion unsafe.

## Canonical owner and approach

Deepen the existing Flow retention domain types into one typed Flow run-history policy owner. A local policy is either absent (inherit the complete parent policy) or a complete pair of mode plus days. Most-specific complete policy wins. Organization is an inherited default, not a hidden hard maximum.

The first implementation slice supports:
- preserve: data becomes eligible after days but only an explicit administrator purge can remove it;
- review_required: eligible data appears in a read-only due list and can only be removed after explicit approval in the purge use case.

Do not persist automatic until the same slice can safely activate and execute it.

Use dedicated relational Organization, Space, and Flow run-history policy columns with constraints preventing partial pairs. Backfill every existing non-null duration as preserve. Add dedicated Organization-admin-only operational read/write interfaces that work for draft and published Flows. Remove retention writes from Flow definition authoring and stop using Spaces.data_retention_days as the Flow policy owner. Reuse existing authorization, AuditService, generated-client pipeline, and effective projection.

## In scope

- typed mode/days invariants, complete inheritance, effective source, contributors, and projection;
- zero-surprise migration and rollback notes;
- admin-only Organization, Space, and Flow policy configuration;
- published-Flow policy changes without changing published definition content;
- policy create/change/clear audit records with bounded metadata;
- generated OpenAPI/client contract and administrator UX;
- removal of the old authoring write path and misleading Space coupling.

## Non-goals

No automatic scheduler or automatic enum value; no destructive purge execution; no organization hard guardrail; no legal-hold/classification engine; no delegated Space-manager or Flow-editor authority; no per-category policy matrix; no generalized tenancy or retention framework; no Flow AI Builder source change.

## Acceptance criteria

- A scope stores both mode and days or neither; database and typed validation reject partial policy state.
- Flow inherits Space, Space inherits Organization, and a complete most-specific override may lengthen or shorten the default.
- Organization automatic/30, Space automatic/60, Flow automatic/90 is the future hierarchy contract, but this slice exposes only preserve/review_required.
- Existing Organization, Space, and Flow days migrate to preserve with identical eligibility thresholds and no new deletion, job, or notification.
- Space Flow policy no longer depends on generic conversation retention.
- Only Organization administrators may create, replace, or clear policies at all scopes.
- Published and draft Flows accept operational policy changes; ordinary Flow definition updates cannot change retention.
- Policy saves and clears are audited without Flow content, prompts, files, signed URLs, secrets, or provider payloads.
- Read projections and generated types expose effective policy, source, and complete contributors.
- Policy changes never enqueue or perform deletion.

## TDD and validation

Write RED proofs for complete inheritance, partial-state rejection, migration backfill, cross-scope resolution, admin authorization, published-Flow updates, ordinary-editor denial, audit attribution/redaction, OpenAPI/generated contract, and visible administrator behavior. Run focused backend domain/integration tests, migration upgrade/downgrade tests, Ruff, Pyright, route metadata, generated SDK tests, web tests, frontend check/build, and i18n validation.

## Risk and recovery

Schema and public-contract changes can strand partial rows or churn generated clients. Preflight current values, use additive/backfill/constrain ordering, inspect generated diffs, and keep downgrade explicit. Rollback restores the days-only projection while preserving values; it must never enable deletion. Policy controls can be feature-hidden without losing stored settings.

## Allowed ownership paths

backend/src/eneo/flows/**; backend/src/eneo/database/tables/{flow_tables.py,tenant_table.py,space_table.py}; backend/src/eneo/settings/** only for the existing Organization Flow settings interface; backend/src/eneo/spaces/** only for the dedicated Flow policy adapter; backend/migrations/**; focused backend Flow/settings/space/OpenAPI tests; frontend/packages/eneo-js generated contract; frontend/apps/web Flow/admin retention routes, feature state, translations, and focused tests. Do not edit Flow AI Builder modules.

## Evidence

- backend/src/eneo/data_retention/infrastructure/data_retention_service.py:166-177 resolves days only.
- backend/src/eneo/flows/domain/flow.py:180-212 has no execution mode.
- backend/src/eneo/flows/application/flow_service.py:200-269 couples retention to draft definition writes.
- backend/src/eneo/spaces/api/space_models.py:131-147 reuses generic conversation retention.
- frontend/apps/web/src/lib/features/flows/flowEditorRetention.ts:23-28 prevents a first override when no policy exists.
- Opus planning session flow-retention-policy-ux gave the revised plan green at score 8.

Confidence: high.

title: Run Flow purges automatically only after explicit activation
description:
TL;DR: Add automatic Flow run-history purging only as an explicit administrator-selected policy mode, using the same bounded and audited purge owner as manual and review-approved deletion.

## Problem and operator impact

Administrators need automatic deletion for real storage-limitation obligations, but entering a duration must never enable it. Shipping a persisted automatic value before safe execution exists creates a dangerous dead contract; building a second scheduler-only deletion path creates duplicate ownership.

## Canonical owner and approach

Add automatic to the typed Flow run-history policy only in the slice that also ships activation safety and runtime enforcement. Reuse FlowRunPurgeService from flows-1z1.3 for preview, locks, reference checks, bounded batches, idempotency, status, recovery, and immutable receipts. Add one narrow scheduled selector/dispatcher, not a retention framework.

A complete automatic policy is explicitly saved by an Organization administrator at Organization, Space, or Flow scope. Most-specific complete policy wins. Saving or shortening a policy never deletes backlog immediately. Activation requires a bounded impact preview, explicit acknowledgement, reason, re-authentication at the existing high-risk seam if available, notification, and a grace period showing the first deletion time.

## Acceptance criteria

- Automatic is never inferred from a duration, inherited as a partial field, or backfilled from existing settings.
- Existing and newly migrated policies remain preserve until an administrator explicitly selects automatic.
- Review-required overdue data remains preserved and escalated; it never falls through to automatic.
- Automatic/30 at Organization, automatic/60 at Space, and automatic/90 at one Flow deletes that Flow at 90, other Flows in the Space at 60, and other Spaces at 30.
- Clearing a child override into inherited automatic shows and confirms the exact resulting automatic policy.
- Switching automatic to preserve/review stops future starts immediately; already-running bounded operations expose status and explicit cancellation/recovery semantics.
- Scheduler dispatch uses the same purge module and cannot widen the preview/fingerprint set.
- Destructive transitions and receipts are transactionally auditable; audit failure prevents protected deletion state from committing.
- Failure never silently retries forever or broadens scope. Resumption/recovery follows the explicit purge operation contract.
- Query selection is bounded and measured with representative cardinality before release.
- No generic scheduler, policy DSL, legal-hold system, or per-category mode matrix is added.

## Dependencies

Requires the complete policy foundation, explicit purge use case, audit completeness, and verified backup/object/provider deletion semantics. Automatic remains unavailable until every dependency is green.

## Tests and validation

TDD covers explicit activation, authorization, grace period, inherited automatic confirmation, backlog non-deletion on save, schedule selection, bounded dispatch, duplicate start, crash/recovery, audit failure, blockers, deactivation, and immutable receipts. Apply Python performance measurement to the production selector and purge interface with representative query plans/cardinality. Run backend/runtime/migration/API/client/frontend/i18n suites and release failure-injection checks.

## Risk and recovery

This is irreversible and should ship disabled until activation and purge contracts pass. Rollback disables new automatic dispatch while retaining policies, operation status, and receipts; in-flight operations remain visible and recoverable. Never fall back to the old daily DataRetentionService orchestration.

## Non-goals

No Flow AI Builder session deletion policy, generic platform retention engine, organization hard maximum, records classification, or generalized tenancy layer.

Confidence: high on architecture; execution remains blocked by dependencies.

title: Preserve Flow runtime input files across worker restarts
description:
TL;DR: Define and prove what happens to uploaded Flow step input files when a
worker restarts a step as a new attempt. A restart must either reuse the original
immutable input-file bindings deliberately or fail with one explicit terminal
reason; it must never silently execute with an empty input.

## Problem

Run creation binds uploaded step input files to attempt 1, while the executor
allocates the next persisted attempt number after a worker restart. Runtime input
lookup is exact by attempt number. The repository no longer has the predecessor
copy API that stale integration fixtures still call. This leaves restart behavior
undefined and may cause a restarted file-backed step to see no files.

## Canonical owner and approach

`FlowRunRepository` owns persisted attempt/file binding and `FlowExecutor` owns
restart orchestration. First reproduce the restart through the supported worker
entry point. Then choose one explicit invariant in those owners: immutable run
input bindings are deliberately inherited by the new attempt, or restart is
terminalized before provider execution with a typed public/operator error.

Prefer reusing the persisted source binding over restoring a generic predecessor
copy helper. Do not reintroduce retired manual rerun behavior or add a retry
framework.

## Acceptance criteria

- A worker restart after attempt 1 has a documented, typed input-file outcome.
- A restarted file-backed step cannot call its handler/provider with an empty
  file list when the original run had bound files.
- Any inherited binding remains tenant/run/step scoped, ordered, idempotent, and
  auditable as the new attempt's exact execution input.
- Duplicate delivery and another crash converge without duplicate file rows or
  a different effective input.
- Unsupported restart is terminalized with one typed, redacted failure instead
  of silently degrading.
- Stale fixtures using `predecessor_attempt_id` and
  `copy_step_input_files_from_predecessor_attempt` are replaced only after the
  supported behavior is proven.

## Tests and validation

- PostgreSQL integration test: create a run with uploaded step files, persist a
  failed/interrupted first attempt, start the worker again, and assert the exact
  effective input and attempt evidence.
- Crash/duplicate-start test for idempotency and row uniqueness.
- Runtime test proving provider execution is not reached with missing files.
- Ruff, Pyright, Flow runtime unit/integration suite.

## Evidence

- `backend/src/eneo/flows/infrastructure/flow_run_repo.py:447-472` seeds uploaded
  input-file rows with `attempt_no=1` during run creation.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/runtime/executor.py:1048-1070` allocates the next attempt
  number on step start.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/runtime/executor.py:1527-1541` requests input files for
  that exact attempt.
- `backend/src/eneo/flows/infrastructure/flow_run_repo.py:1683-1705` queries exact
  `run_id`, tenant, step, and attempt.
- `backend/tests/integration/flows/test_flow_run_listing_and_evidence_measurement.py:310-331`
  still calls removed predecessor/copy APIs, exposing the unresolved contract.

## Out of scope

- No user-triggered rerun feature.
- No general executor rewrite or state-machine framework.
- No Flow AI Builder changes and no new multi-tenancy architecture.

Confidence: high that the contract is unresolved; implementation choice must be
confirmed by the supported worker-restart behavior test.

title: Let administrators preview and explicitly run Flow purges
description:
TL;DR: Add one tenant-administrator-only Flow purge use case with side-effect-free preview, explicit confirmation, durable operation status, bounded execution, manual resume, and an immutable audit receipt.

## Problem

The current code can safely select and purge Flow records, but only scheduled cleanup orchestrates it. Administrators need an explicit control that shows impact before deletion and never runs merely because a policy changed. Abandoned uploads must be a named scope because no run-scoped purge can ever select them.

## Canonical owner and approach

- FlowRunHistoryPurgeRepository remains the canonical owner of locks, delete-time rechecks, shared-file protection, and atomic batch persistence.
- Add one concrete FlowRunPurgeService as the application owner of preview, start, resume, and receipt semantics.
- Move Flow selection/orchestration from DataRetentionService into that service and delete the old methods in the same slice; retain no facade or Protocol.
- Use the existing tenant-admin Flow settings adapter and generated client for preview/start/status/resume.
- Register one explicitly enqueued long-running function on the existing maintenance worker; do not create a job framework.
- Persist one flow_purge_operations record with operation ID, tenant, typed scope, effective policy snapshot, preview as_of, deterministic fingerprint, status, bounded progress counts, reason, principal, timestamps, and sanitized failure. Add a partial unique index allowing at most one active purge operation per tenant, regardless of scope.

## Minimal preview and execution contract

Scope names each destructive category separately:
- run history and its result/evidence/file/outbox/checkpoint records;
- abandoned runtime uploads;
- debug evidence redaction;
- soft-deleted template assets;
- optionally finalizable soft-deleted Flows in the dependent finalization slice.

Fingerprint is a deterministic hash of tenant, typed scope, effective tenant/Space/Flow policy values, and preview as_of. Execution re-runs the same eligibility selection bounded by preview as_of; later runs or policy broadening cannot widen the deletion set. Delete-time locks and audit/webhook/reference blockers still recheck and may only shrink actual deletion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Preview is side-effect free and reports as_of, effective scope/cutoff/policy sources, candidate runs, files, bytes, abandoned uploads, debug evidence, template assets, optional finalizable Flows, lock deferrals, undelivered-audit blockers, and unresolved-webhook blockers.
- Execute requires tenant-admin authorization, mandatory bounded reason, explicit acknowledgement, and a matching unexpired fingerprint.
- Replayed starts are idempotent. A tenant can have at most one active purge operation across all scopes; a competing start returns a conflict that identifies the existing operation without enqueueing work.
- Execution is bounded and retry-safe, and starts only after the administrator request.
- Worker crash marks the operation failed_resumable; nothing automatically resumes or re-enqueues deletion. A tenant administrator must explicitly resume the same operation.
- Status exposes pending/running/completed/failed_resumable/cancelled plus bounded progress and sanitized errors.
- Completion emits one immutable receipt containing requested versus actual counts/bytes, blockers, principal, reason, timestamps, policy snapshot, scope, and operation ID.
- Shared files and protected references remain intact.
- Existing source has tenant/Space/Flow eligibility plus debug-evidence policy; no nonexistent classification/hold hierarchy is invented.
- Generated API/client types are the only frontend contract source.
- The existing Flow settings page supports preview, confirmation, start, progress, failure, and explicit resume.
- No generic deletion framework, generic job framework, public tenant-member API, or direct SQL procedure is added.

## Tests and validation

PostgreSQL contracts:
- preview non-mutation and category counts;
- stale fingerprint and policy-change rejection;
- as_of prevents a broadened/new deletion set;
- duplicate start and competing operation;
- worker crash then admin resume;
- lock deferral, shared file, undelivered audit, unresolved webhook;
- abandoned upload selection;
- exactly one receipt.

API/client/frontend contracts:
- tenant-admin authorization and tenant isolation;
- validation/conflict/error shapes and operation IDs;
- OpenAPI/generated client;
- destructive confirmation, progress, failure/resume, translated copy.

Commands:

- cd backend && uv run pyright
- cd frontend && bun run --filter '@eneo/eneo-js' test
- cd frontend && bun run --filter '@eneo/web' test
- cd frontend && bun run check && bun run build

## Risk and recovery

This is destructive and migration-visible. Ship execution disabled until preview/authorization/audit contracts pass. Rollback disables new start/resume actions while preserving operation records and receipts; never re-enable scheduled purging.

## Out of scope

No cross-product purge console, recurrence, public Flow API, classification-retention system that is absent from current source, or rewrite of file ownership.

## Evidence

Reviewed tree a65083bac7731537bc53f6e627370c4370a7b224:

title: Finalize deleted Flows only when an administrator includes them
description:

title: Prevent stale recovery from invalidating durable webhooks
description:
TL;DR: Make stale-run discovery and terminalizing mutation share one SQL predicate so a newly durable pending or claimed webhook prevents stale recovery from failing the run.

## Problem

Discovery excludes stale running runs with pending webhook delivery, but terminalize_run_status later checks only status and updated_at. A webhook can become durable between SELECT and UPDATE, leaving run and outbox lifecycles inconsistent.

## Canonical owner and approach

stale_running_flow_run_predicate remains the only SQL policy owner. When stale_before is supplied, FlowRunRepository.terminalize_run_status composes that exact predicate. FlowRunTerminalizer remains the lifecycle owner.

title: Separate Flow AI Builder session retention before production
description:
TL;DR: Flow AI Builder conversation sessions currently inherit generic Space/conversation retention and can be deleted by the daily worker. Make that privacy-sensitive behavior an explicit Builder-owned product decision before production.

## Problem and user impact

BuilderSessions persist the AI Builder conversation JSONB and can contain prompts, planning state, generated specifications, and sensitive K3-type working material. The 03:00 data-retention worker currently deletes expired Builder sessions using the effective Space/Organization conversation duration. That is not an explicit Builder-specific opt-in and is separate from Flow run-history retention.

Broad statements such as “nothing Flow-related is automatically deleted” are therefore false. The behavior may surprise administrators who set conversation retention without understanding that Builder working sessions are included.

## Canonical owner and recommendation

The Flow AI Builder workstream owns Builder session lifecycle and retention. Separate it from both Flow run-history policy and generic conversation retention. Existing Builder sessions and inherited values should default to preserve. Give Organization administrators a Builder-specific complete policy with preserve and review-required first; add automatic only together with explicit activation, safe bounded deletion, audit, recovery, and truthful storage semantics.

Reuse the platform administrator authorization and audit vocabulary, but do not route Builder deletion through FlowRunPurgeService and do not create a generic cross-product retention framework.

## Acceptance criteria

- The current scheduled behavior is explicitly approved and disclosed or disabled before production; absence of a Builder policy never triggers deletion.
- Existing generic conversation/Space durations do not silently become automatic Builder deletion.
- Builder policy changes are Organization-admin-only, audited, and visible with effective source and next action.
- Review-required overdue sessions remain preserved until approval.
- Automatic, if shipped, requires explicit activation, preview/backlog impact, grace period, notification, bounded retry-safe deletion, and immutable receipt.
- Active or recoverable Builder sessions have explicit protection rules; lock expiry alone does not make sensitive working state unexpectedly disposable.
- Audit metadata contains identifiers/counts/outcomes, never conversation content, prompts, files, credentials, or provider payloads.
- Flow proper tests and product copy remain scoped to Flow run history rather than claiming Builder behavior.
- The implementation is owned and validated in the AI Builder worktree; this Flow-proper branch performs no Builder source edits.
